143: \begin{abstract}
144: Hadronic decays of boosted resonances, e.g., top quark jets, at hadronic super colliders
145: are frequent predictions in TeV-scale extensions of the Standard Model of Particle Physics.
146: In such scenarios, accurate modeling of QCD radiation is necessary for trustworthy predictions.
147: We present the automation of fully differential, next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD corrections with parton shower (PS) matching for 
148: an effective  Left-Right Symmetric Model (LRSM) that features $W_R^\pm, Z_R$ gauge bosons and heavy Majorana neutrinos $N$.
149: Publicly available universal model files require remarkably fewer user inputs for predicting benchmark collider processes
150: than leading order LRSM constructions. 
151: We present predictions for inclusive $W_R^\pm, Z_R$ production at the $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV Large Hadron Collider (LHC)
152: and a hypothetical future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider (VLHC),
153: as well as inclusive $N$ production for a hypothetical Large Hadron Electron Collider (LHeC).
154: As a case study, we investigate at NLO+PS accuracy the properties of 
155: heavy neutrino (color-singlet) jets and top quark (color-triplet) jets from decays of high-mass $W_R$ bosons at the LHC.
156: Contrary to top jets, we find that the kinematic properties of heavy neutrinos jets, and in particular jet mass, 
157: are resilient against the effects of parton showers and hard QCD radiation.
158: This suggests that in searches for neutrino jets, 
159: aggressive selection cuts that would otherwise be inappropriate for top jets can be imposed with minimal signal loss.
160: \end{abstract}

168: \section{Introduction}
169: The Left Right Symmetric Model (LRSM)~\cite{Pati:1974yy,Mohapatra:1974gc,Senjanovic:1975rk} 
170: is an economic and well-defined solution to a number discrepancies within the Standard Model of particle physics (SM).
171:  Such issues include: the origin and lightness of neutrino masses, the existence of dark matter, and 
172: the baryon-antibaryon asymmetry of the universe.
173: 
174: The model, based on the gauge group
175: \begin{equation}
176:  {\rm SU}(3)_c \otimes {\rm SU}(2)_L \otimes {\rm SU}(2)_R \otimes {\rm U}(1)_{B-L},
177: \end{equation}
178: predicts {right-handed (RH) currents and the existence of heavy, RH gauge bosons $W_R^\pm$ and $Z_R$. In addition,} the model contains 
179:  three RH neutrinos $N_R$ that are charged under ${\rm SU}(2)_R \otimes {\rm U}(1)_{B-L}$ but singlets under SM symmetries.
180: For masses up to several TeV, the LRSM can be tested at {collider experiments such as the Large Hadron Collider (LHC)}  through searches for processes like
181: \begin{eqnarray}
182:  p ~p \rightarrow	& \WR^\pm	& \rightarrow tb ~\text{or}~ N_R \ell^\pm, ~
183:  \quad\text{with}\quad N_R \rightarrow 	\ell^\pm W_R^{\mp *}  \rightarrow \ell^\pm q \overline{q'},
184:  \quad\text{and}
185:  \label{eq:ppWRff}
186:  \\
187:  p ~p \rightarrow	& \ZR		& \rightarrow t\overline{t} ~\text{or}~ N_R N_R,
188:  \quad\text{with}\quad \ell \in\{e,\mu,\tau\}, \quad q\in\{u,c,d,s,t,b\},
189:   \label{eq:ppZRff}
190: \end{eqnarray}
191: and are shown diagrammatically in Fig.~\ref{fig:production}.
192: The channels lead to {the distinct}  
193: $\ell^\pm\ell^\pm +nj$~\cite{Keung:1983uu}, $\ell^\pm+j$~\cite{Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov}, and single top~\cite{Simmons:1996ws} topologies, 
194: and have been studied 
195: extensively~\cite{Han:2012vk,Chen:2013fna,Vasquez:2014mxa,Ng:2015hba,Dev:2015kca,Kang:2015uoc,FileviezPerez:2016erl,
196:   Frank:2010cj,Tello:2010am, Das:2012ii,  Maiezza:2015lza,Gluza:2015goa,Chakrabortty:2016wkl,Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov,Simmons:1996ws}.

216: Monte Carlo (MC) modeling of the above processes by LHC experiments typically~\cite{Aad:2015xaa,Khachatryan:2014dka,ATLAS:2015nsi,Khachatryan:2015dcf}
217: involve leading order (LO) simulations matched to parton showers (PS)
218: and are normalized with constant factors, so-called $K$-factors, to account for QCD corrections.
219: 
220: While sufficient for predicting total inclusive cross sections,
221: the procedure does not correctly capture the kinematic changes 
222: induced  by high-transverse momentum $(p_T)$
223: initial-state radiation (ISR) or final-state radiation (FSR). 
224: This can substantially impact experimental sensitivity,
225: particularly as $\WR~(\ZR)$ decays to top quarks involve up to four (six) energetic jets at LO.
226: 
227: Jet matching schemes at a scale $\mu\ll M_{V_R}$, for $V_{R} = \WR,\ZR$,  can alleviate such problems.
228: However, missing virtual corrections give rise to potentially unstable soft/collinear logarithms of the 
229: form $\alpha_s(\MVR^2)\log(\MVR^2/\mu^{2})$ that spoil perturbative convergence for sufficiently large $(\MVR/\mu)$ ratios.
230: 
231: Furthermore, decays of high-mass RH gauge bosons to top quarks and heavy neutrinos can give rise to 
232: top~\cite{Baur:2007ck,Thaler:2008ju,Kaplan:2008ie} and heavy neutrino~\cite{Mitra:2016kov} jets, 
233: which carry different color charges, and hence possess different QCD radiation patterns.
234: Observables sensitive to the structure of these jets, e.g., jet mass, can be used to discriminate against SM backgrounds 
235: but require information that first arises with $\mathcal{O}(\as)$ corrections.
236: 
237: 
238: To resolve these complications, 
239: we present the automation of next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD corrections with parton shower (PS) matching for an 
240: effective LRSM, using the FeynRules (FR) + NLOCT + MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO (\mgamc)~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py,Degrande:2014vpa,Alwall:2014hca} 
241: framework.
242: 
243: The universal FR object (UFO) files~\cite{Degrande:2011ua} are publicly available from~\cite{nloFRModel} and require remarkably fewer 
244: inputs for simulating fully differential, benchmark collider processes 
245: than current LO implementations~\cite{Sjostrand:2006za,Ashry:2013loa,Roitgrund:2014zka}.
246: 
247: We demonstrate this by providing predictions for $\WR,\ZR$ production at the $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV LHC 
248: and a future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider (VLHC)~\cite{Arkani-Hamed:2015vfh}.
249: We also present predictions for inclusive $N$ production at a hypothetical Large Hadron Electron Collider (LHeC)~\cite{AbelleiraFernandez:2012cc}.
250: The Born diagrams for these processes are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:dydisProd}.
251: 
252: As a case study, we investigate at NLO+PS accuracy the properties of 
253: heavy neutrino (color-singlet) jets and top quark (color-triplet) jets from decays of high-mass $\WR$ bosons at the LHC.

274: \section{Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model}\label{sec:theory}
275: The Effective LRSM field content consists of the usual SM states, the $\WR^\pm$ and $\ZR$ gauge bosons, 
276: which are aligned with their mass eigenstates, and three heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_i$, 
277: aligned with the RH chiral states.
278: 
279: In the LRSM, the $\WR$ chiral coupling to quarks are given by
280: \begin{eqnarray}
281:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-q-q'} = \frac{-\kappa_R^q g}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j=u,d,\dots}\overline{u}_i V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ d_j + \text{H.c.},
282:  \label{chcurrent}
283: \end{eqnarray}
284: Here, $u_i (d_j)$ is an up-(down-)type quark of flavor $i (j)$; 
285: $P_{R(L)} = \frac{1}{2}(1\pm\gamma^5)$ denotes the RH(LH) chiral projection operator; and
286: $V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}$  is the RH Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix, which is related to the SM CKM matrix.
287: Throughout this study, we will assume five massless quarks and take both the SM and RH CKM matrices to be diagonal with unit entries.
288: $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha_{\rm EM}(M_Z)}/\sin\theta_W$ is the SM Weak coupling constant and 
289: $\kappa_{R}^{q}\in\mathds{R}$ is an overall normalization for the $\WR$ interaction strength.
290: 
291: For leptons, the $\WR$ coupling and leptonic mixing is parametrized by~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Han:2012vk}
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-\ell-\nu/N} = \frac{-\kappa_R^\ell g}{\sqrt{2}}
294:  \sum_{\ell=e,\mu,\tau}
295:  \left[
296:  \sum_{m=1}^3	\overline{\nu^{c}_m} X_{\ell m} ~+~
297:  \sum_{m'=1}^3	\overline{N_{m'}} Y_{\ell m'}
298:  \right] ~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ \ell^-+\text{H.c.}
299: \end{eqnarray}
300: The matrix $Y_{\ell m'} (X_{\ell m})$ quantifies the mixing between 
301: the heavy (light) neutrino mass eigenstate $N_{m'}~(\nu_{m})$
302: and the RH chiral state with corresponding lepton flavor $\ell$. 
303: 
304: The mixing scale as~\cite{Keung:1983uu}
305: \begin{equation}
306: \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(1) \quad\text{and}\quad  
307: \vert X_{\ell m}\vert^2 \sim 1 - \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(m_{\nu_m}/m_{N_{m'}}).
308: \end{equation}
309: As in the quark sector, $\kappa_R^\ell\in\mathds{R}$ independently normalizes the $\WR$ coupling strength to leptons.
310: 
311: At TeV collider scales, both light neutrino masses and light neutrino mixing can be taken to zero.
312: So for simplicity, we take $Y_{\ell m'}$ to  be diagonal with unit entires:
313: \begin{equation}
314:   \vert Y_{e N}\vert = \vert Y_{\mu N_2}\vert = \vert Y_{\tau N_3}\vert = 1, \quad \vert Y_{\rm others}\vert = \vert X_{\ell m}\vert = 0.
315:   \label{eq:lrsmNuMixing}
316: \end{equation}
317: 
318: Mass and mixing assumptions are modifiable in the public model files~\cite{nloFRModel} but requires UFO regeneration.
319: Specifically, do not load the FR restrictions, ``massless.rst'' and ``diagonalCKM.rst''.

345: After LR symmetry breaking, the $W_{R}^{3}$ and $X_{(B-L)}$ gauge states mix and
346: give rise to the massive $Z_{R}$ and massless (hypercharge) $B$ bosons.
347: 
348: Subsequently, all fermions with $(B-L)$ charges, including $\nu_L$ and $N_R$, couple to $\ZR$.
349: 
350: For chiral fermion $f$, we parametrize the $\ZR$ neutral currents by
351: \begin{eqnarray}
352:  \mathcal{L}_{\ZR-f-f} &=& \frac{-\kappa_{R}^f g}{\sqrt{1 - \left(1/\kappa_{R}^f\right)^2\tWSq}}\sum_{f=u,e,\dots}
353:  \overline{f} Z_{R \mu} \gamma^\mu \left(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}P_L + g_{R}^{\ZR,f}P_R\right)f.
354: \label{neucurrent}
355: \end{eqnarray}
356: $\kappa_{R}^{f}$ are the same $\kappa_{R}^{q,\ell}$ as for $\WR$.
357: In terms of electric and isospin charges, the chiral coefficients are
358: \begin{eqnarray}
359:  g_{L}^{\ZR,f} &=& \left(T_{L}^{3,f} - Q^f\right)\frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq,
360:  \\
361:  g_{R}^{\ZR,f} &=& T_{R}^{3,f} - \frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq Q^f.
362: \end{eqnarray}
363: SU$(2)_L$, SU$(2)_R$, and U$(1)_{\rm EM}$ quantum number assignments for $f$ are summarize in Tbl.~\ref{tb:qNumbers}.
364: 
365: For generic $\kappa_R^{q,\ell}$ normalizations, the LO $\WR,\ZR$ partial decay widths are then
366: \begin{eqnarray}
367:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{qq'}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
368:  \\
369:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{tb}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
370: 					    \left(1-r_t^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_t^{\WR}\right),
371:  \\
372:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \ell N_{m'}} 	&=&     \vert Y_{\ell N_{m'}}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{\ell 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
373: 					\left(1-r_N^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_N^{\WR}\right),
374: \\
375:  \Gam{\ZR\rightarrow f\overline{f}} &=&   
376:  N_c^f 
377:  \cfrac{\kappa_{\ZR}^{f 2} g^2 \MZR \sqrt{1-4r_f^{\ZR}}}{48\pi\left[1 - (1/\kappa_{R}^f)^2\tWSq\right]}
378:  \nonumber\\
379:  &\times&
380:  \left[(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}+g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1+2r_f^{\ZR})+(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}-g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1-4r_f^{\ZR})\right]
381:  \\
382:  r_i^{V_R} &=& \frac{m_{i}^2}{M_{V_R}^2}.
383: \end{eqnarray}
384: Assuming diagonal quark mixing and lepton mixing in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}), the total $\WR,\ZR$ widths are then
385: \begin{eqnarray}
386:  \Gamma_{\WR} &=& 2\Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb}

431: \subsection{Collider Constraints on Effective LRSM}\label{sec:constrains}
432: Direct and indirect tests place stringent limits on the LRSM. 
433: For a recent review, see~\cite{Mitra:2016kov} and references therein.
434: Current LHC dijet and dileptons+jets searches require ~\cite{Aad:2015xaa,Khachatryan:2014dka,ATLAS:2015nsi,Khachatryan:2015dcf}:
435: \begin{equation}
436:  \MWR > 2.6-2.7\TeV \quad\text{at}\quad 95\% \quad\text{CL~for}\quad\kappa_{R}^{q,\ell}=1.
437: \end{equation}
438: Using the $\MWR-\MZR$ mass relation of Eq.~(\ref{eq:massRelationship}), the subsequently limit on $\MZR$ is: 
439: \begin{equation}
440:  \MZR > 4.4-4.6\TeV \quad\text{at}\quad 95\% \quad\text{CL~for}\quad\kappa_{R}^{q,\ell}=1.
441: \end{equation}
442: Heavy neutrino masses remain unconstrained at colliders for $(m_{N_{m'}} / \MWR) \lesssim 0.1$ 
443: due a breakdown of standard collider searches~\cite{Mitra:2016kov}.
444: 
445: We exploit this latitude and equate the lightest heavy neutrino mass, which we denote for simplicity as $N$ with mass $m_N$, to the top quark mass, $m_t$.
446: For simplicity, we decouple the two remaining heavy neutrinos with unrealistically large masses.
447: We do not advocate such a scenario will be realized in nature.
448: This mass assignment permits us to make a more systematic comparison of heavy neutrino and top jets in Sec.~\ref{sec:jetKin}.
449: 
450: We summarize our choices of LRSM inputs in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmInputs}).

454: \subsection{Limitations of the Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model}\label{sec:modelLimits}
455: The Effective LRSM is sufficient to describe at NLO+PS accuracy resonant production and decay of $\WR,\ZR,$ and $N$ in $pp/ep/ee$ collisions,
456: and in particular the processes listed in Eqs.~(\ref{eq:ppWRff})-(\ref{eq:ppZRff}).
457: This is done with minimal couplings, as seen in Eqs.~(\ref{chcurrent})-(\ref{neucurrent}).
458: A limitation of the model is that it does not extend the SM Higgs sector to include the  LRSM scalar fields.
459: Constraints from flavor changing neutral current processes imply that the LRSM Higgs masses are as heavy as 15-20 TeV,
460: and hence decouple from LHC phenomenology~\cite{Barry:2013xxa,Maiezza:2014ala,Bertolini:2014sua,Maiezza:2016bzp,Mitra:2016kov}.
461: It is this exclusion that gives the Effective LRSM its flexibility.
462: However, as a consequence, non-Abelian $\WR$ and $\ZR$ interactions, as well as their couplings to SM bosons, are ill-defined.
463: Phenomenologically, this implies that most resonant pair production and vector boson scattering processes involving $\WR$ and $\ZR$ 
464: are not correctly modeled.
465: The SM, on the other hand, is fully supported.

478: \section{Computational Setup and Signal Modeling}\label{sec:setup}
479: \subsection{Model Implementation}
480: We implement the SM Lagrangian with Goldstone boson couplings in the Feynman gauge 
481: and the Lagrangian terms of Eqs.~(\ref{chcurrent})-(\ref{neucurrent}) in the Unitary gauge
482: into FR 2.3.10~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py}.
483: $R_2$ rational and QCD renormalization counter terms are calculated with~\nloct~1.02~\cite{Degrande:2014vpa} and FeynArts 3.8~\cite{Hahn:2000kx}.
484: UFO model files are publicly available from the FR model database~\cite{nloFRModel}, 
485: and can be ported into modern event generators, including
486: \mgamc~\cite{Alwall:2014hca},
487: HERWIG~\cite{Bellm:2015jjp}, and SHERPA~\cite{Gleisberg:2008ta}.
488: 
489: \subsection{Monte Carlo Configuration}
490: Fully differential results at LO and NLO are obtained using \mgamc~\confirm{2.5.$\beta$2}~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}.
491: Events are parton showered and hadronized using Pythia~\confirm{8.219} (PY8)~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea},
492: and passed to MadAnalysis5~\confirm{v1.4}~\cite{Conte:2012fm} for particle-level clustering.
493: Unless stated otherwise, jets are clustered via FastJet~\confirm{3.2.1}~\cite{Cacciari:2005hq,Cacciari:2011ma} 
494: according to the anti-$k_T$ algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2008gp} with a separation scale of $R = 0.4$.
495: 
496: LRSM inputs are given in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmInputs}). SM inputs are taken from the 2014 Particle Data Group~\cite{Agashe:2014kda}:
497: \begin{eqnarray}
498:  \alpha^{\rm \overline{MS}}(M_{Z}) = 1/127.940, \quad 
499:  M_{Z} = 91.1876\GeV, \quad
500:  \sin^{2}_{\rm \overline{MS}}(\theta_{W}) = 0.23126.
501:  \label{eq:smInputs}
502: \end{eqnarray}
503: We use the NLO NNPDF3.0 parton distribution function (PDF) set~(\texttt{lhaid=260000})~\cite{Ball:2014uwa} for LO and NLO calculations.
504: PDFs and $\as(\mu_r)$ are extracted using LHAPDF 6.1.6~\cite{Buckley:2014ana}.
505: 
506: For all processes, we equate the renormalization $(\mu_r)$ and factorization $(\mu_f)$ scales.
507: We choose as a dynamical scale, half the sum over all final-state transverse energies:
508: \begin{equation}
509:  \mu_r, \mu_f = \mu_0 \equiv \sum_{k=N,\ell,\text{jets}}\cfrac{E_{T,k}}{2} = \frac12\sum_{k} \sqrt{m_k^2 + p_{T,k}^2}
510:  \label{eq:mgScale}
511: \end{equation}
512: At NLO, we estimate the residual uncertainty from missing higher order terms by simultaneously varying $\mu_{r},\mu_f$ over the range:
513: \begin{equation}
514:  0.5\times\mu_0 ~<~ \mu_{r},\mu_f ~<~ 2\times\mu_0.
515: \end{equation}
516: 
517: 
518: Instructions for using the Effective LRSM at NLO within the \mgamc~framework are provided in App.~\ref{app:sigDef}.
519: 
520: For total inclusive cross sections reported in Sec.~\ref{sec:ppXSec} and \ref{sec:epXSec}, no phase space cuts are applied.
521: 
522: To study the properties of $N$ jets and $t$ jets, we consider the processes 
523: \begin{equation}
524:  p ~p ~\rightarrow \WR^{\pm (*)} ~\rightarrow Ne^\pm, ~tb, ~\text{and}~q\overline{q'}, \quad\text{for}\quad q\in\{u,d,c,s\}, 
525:  \label{eq:lhcNLOPSprocesses}
526: \end{equation}
527: at NLO in QCD. We include hard QCD radiation off the final-state quarks and a finite $\WR$ width.
528: While we neglect interference with the SM $W$ for simplicity, it is possible to implement it within our framework.
529: To minimize the contamination of far off-shell $\WR$ with virtualities $Q^2\ll \MWR^{2}$,
530: we impose a generator-level cut on $X\in\{N,t,q\}$ and require $p_T^X > 750\GeV$.
531: While the cut on light quarks is trivial in \mgamc
532: restrictions on on-shell heavy neutrinos and top quarks require implementing a user-defined cut into the phase space integration routine.
533: This can be done in a straightforward manner; see App.~\ref{app:GenCuts} for instructions.

535: \subsection{Spin-Correlated Decays of $N$ and $t$ with Improved MadSpin}
536: We decay $N$ and $t$ via MadSpin~\cite{Artoisenet:2012st}, thus retaining full spin correlation, just before parton showering.
537: However, three body decays like $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm\WR^{\mp*}\rightarrow\ell^\pm q\overline{q'}$ are not supported in current releases of MadSpin.
538: Therefore, we have implemented an extension of the code to support such subprocesses.
539: 
540: To achieve this, we first use a standard MC technique to generate unweighted decay events with the parent particle being exactly on-shell.
541: Those events are then boosted to match the decaying particle of the production event.
542: Obviously such samples lack spin-correlations between the production event and the decay event.
543: To include spin effects, one can re-weight each decayed event by the following ratio:
544: \begin{equation}
545: \cfrac{|M_{P+D}|^2}{|M_P|^2|M_D|^2},
546: \end{equation}
547: where $\vert M_P\vert^2$, $\vert M_D\vert^2$ and$|M_{P+D}|^2$ are, respectively, 
548: the matrix-element squared for the production event, the decay event, and the decayed production event.
549: In order to keep unweighted events after such re-weighting, we follow the MadSpin strategy of keeping 
550: the same production event and try associating it with different decay events as long as none of them pass the unweighting criteria.
551: 
552: This feature will be include in \mgamc~2.5.3  and is currently available on request. 
553: The syntax for enacting such decays is provided in App.~\ref{app:MadSpin}.
554: 
555: We note that is also presently possible to perform the three-body heavy $N$ decay with PY8, but at the cost of neglecting spin corrections.

691: Proposed multi-TeV deeply inelastic scattering (DIS) experiments, such as the LHeC~\cite{AbelleiraFernandez:2012cc} and eRHIC~\cite{Aschenauer:2014cki},
692: are well-motivated and can greatly improve our knowledge of PDFs at low- and high-$x$, resummed QCD, and EW couplings.
693: 
694: Additionally, due to the cleanliness of the collider environment (in comparison to $pp$ collisions) and the increased c.m.e~reach over the LHC, 
695: the LHeC offers a complementary opportunity to search for new physics.
696: 
697: In particular, the LHeC is capable of probing regions of LRSM parameter space inaccessible to the 
698: LHC~\cite{Blaksley:2011ey,Duarte:2014zea,Mondal:2015zba,Lindner:2016lxq}.
699: 
700: The LRSM can be tested at the LHeC through searches for heavy $N$ through the process,
701: \begin{equation}
702:  e^- p ~\rightarrow ~N ~j ~+~ X,	\quad\text{where}\quad 		N\rightarrow \ell^{'\pm}q\overline{q'},
703:  \label{eq:disProcess}
704: \end{equation}
705: which is mediated by $t$-channel $\WR$ exchange and is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:feynmanDIS}.
706: 
707: Initial search strategies~\cite{Mondal:2015zba,Lindner:2016lxq} have proposed requiring three high-$p_T$ jets in the central region of the detector.
708: Two arise from the decay of $N$, the third from the associated $\WR$ exchange.
709: 
710: We argue that the requirement of a third jet is unnecessary and likely reduces $N$ discovery potential:
711: Eq.~(\ref{eq:disProcess}) involves the exchange of a gauge boson with a mass much larger than the collider, 
712: and hence momentum transfer scale, i.e., $\MWR^2\gg \vert\hat{t}\vert$.
713: This implies that the spectator jet has no natural momentum scale, unlike the decay products of $N$, which scale like $m_N$.
714: Subsequently, a large (and entirely finite) region of the phase space is populated by forward, low-$p_T$ jets that do not satisfy the selection 
715: criteria of~\cite{Mondal:2015zba,Lindner:2016lxq}. 
716: 
717: Furthermore, this spectator is not necessary to reconstruct the heavy neutrino momentum.
718: We therefore recommend a more inclusive approach, and propose instead the search 
719: \begin{equation}
720:   e^- ~p ~\rightarrow ~N ~+~\text{X}, \quad\text{where}\quad 		N\rightarrow \ell^{'\pm}q\overline{q'}.
721:   \label{eq:disNinc}
722: \end{equation}

746: \subsection{Kinematics of Neutrino and Top Jets at NLO+PS in LHC Collisions}\label{sec:jetKin}
747: Heavy neutrinos and top quarks originating from $\WR$ (or $\ZR$) decays carry characteristic transverse momenta that scale as 
748: $p_T\sim \MWR/2$. For $\MWR\gg m_{N,t}$, such neutrinos and tops are highly Lorentz boosted.
749: Subsequently, their decays to leptons and/or quarks, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:Decay}, are highly collimated,
750: and lead to the formation of heavy neutrino jets~\cite{Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov} and top quark jets~\cite{Baur:2007ck,Thaler:2008ju,Kaplan:2008ie}.
751: 
752: In this section we compare kinematics of neutrino, top, and light quark jets from high-mass $\MWR$ decays at NLO+PS accuracy.
753: 
754: We describe our computational setup in Sec.~\ref{sec:setup}.
755: 
756: The $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm q\overline{q'}$ branching fraction is 100\%; for $t$, we allow both hadronic and leptonic decays of the SM $W$.
757: 
758: 
759: 
760: Events topologies are studied by first identifying charged lepton candidates, 
761: then clustering all residual objects, including potentially misidentified leptons, into jets.
762: 
763: Stable charged leptons $\ell\in\{e,\mu\}$ are considered hadronically isolated if 
764: the scalar sum of transverse energy $(E_T)$ over all neighboring hadrons $X$ within a distance of $\Delta R_{\ell X}<0.3$
765: is less than $10\%$ of the lepton's $E_T$, i.e.,
766: \begin{equation}
767: \sum_{X\in\{\text{hadrons}\}} E_{T}^{X} / E_{T}^{\ell} < 0.1~\quad\text{for}\quad~\Delta R_{\ell X} < 0.3.
768: \end{equation}
769: 
770: At the 13 TeV LHC, charged lepton candidates are then defined as hadronically isolated leptons that meet the following kinematic, 
771: fiducial, and lepton isolation requirements~\cite{CMS:2015kjy}:
772: \begin{equation}
773: p_T^{\ell} > 35\GeV, ~\quad \vert \eta^\ell\vert < 2.4, ~\quad \Delta R_{\ell\ell'} > 0.3.
774: \end{equation}
775: 
776: We cluster all remaining constituents into jets according to the 
777: Cambridge/Aachen (C/A) algorithm~\cite{Dokshitzer:1997in,Wobisch:1998wt} with a separation scale of $R = 1.0$.
778: 
779: We ignore clustered jets with $p_T<20\GeV$~\cite{ATLAS:2016ecs}.
780: 
781: Charged leptons and jets are ordered according to their $p_T$ (hardness), with $p_{T}^{j_i} > p_{T}^{j_{(i+1)}}$.
782: 
783: To select for top quarks and heavy neutrinos, we apply the following mass cut on the hardest jet, $j_1$:
784: \begin{equation}
785:   \vert m_{j_1} - m_t \vert  < 25\GeV.
786: \end{equation}
787: The NLO+PS \-accurate cross section before and after the jet mass cut are:
788: \begin{eqnarray}
789:   \sigma^{\rm NLOPS}:\qquad	& 14.0~(36.7)~[76.3]\fb	&			\quad\text{for~the }~	N~(t)~[q]	\quad\text{channel},\\
790:   \sigma^{\rm NLOPS+\text{$m_j$}~Cut}:\qquad	& 8.39~(9.69)~[9.16]\fb	&	\quad\text{for~the }~	N~(t)~[q]	\quad\text{channel}
791: \end{eqnarray}
792: We see that the $m_j$ (accidentally) brings the individual rates to a very comparable level, avoid the need for any additional type of normalization.
793: Without the cut, the quark channels are much larger due to branching fractions that are $3-6\times$ larger.
794: 
795: To reconstruct $\WR$ kinematics, we drop the jet mass cut and sum the momenta of the two hardest jets
796: in the quark channels, or hardest jet and lepton in the neutrino channel.
797: 
798: 
799: 
800: \begin{figure}[!t]
801: \begin{center}
802: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{nDecay_WR_lqq.eps}	\label{fig:nDecay}}
803: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{tDecay_WL_bqq.eps}	\label{fig:tDecay}}
804: \end{center}
805: \caption{Leading decay modes for (a) $N$ and (b) $t$ in the LRSM.} 
806: \label{fig:Decay}
807: \end{figure}
808: 
809: 
810: In Fig.~\ref{fig:lhcKinematics} we plot at NLO+PS accuracy, the differential distributions of various observables related to  $j_1$ 
811: in $\WR$ production and decay to heavy neutrino (solid), top quark (dash), and light quark (dot) jets, at the $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV LHC.
812: 
813: For observable $\mathcal{O}$, the lower panel shows the differential NLO+PS $K$-factor, defined as the ratio
814: \begin{equation}
815:  K^{\rm NLOPS}_{\mathcal{O}} \equiv \cfrac{d\sigma^{\rm NLO+PS}/d\mathcal{O}}{d\sigma^{\rm LO+PS}/d\mathcal{O}}.
816: \end{equation}
817: 
818: \begin{figure}[!t]
819: \begin{center}
820: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTj1.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTj1}	}
821: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_yj1.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_yj1}	}
822: \\
823: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1}	}
824: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1Hemi1.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1Hemi1}	}
825: \end{center}
826: \caption{
827: Differential distributions with respect to (a) $p_T^{j_1}$, (b) $y^{j_1}$, (c) $m_{j_1}$, and the (d)  $m_{j_1}/M_{\rm Hemisphere}$ ratio,
828: at NLO+PS, of $\WR$ production and decay to heavy neutrino (solid), top quark (dash), and light quark (dot) jets, at the $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV LHC.
829: $m_{j_1}$ cut applied.
830: Lower: NLO+PS-to-LO+PS ratio.
831: } 
832: \label{fig:lhcKinematics}
833: \end{figure}
834: 
835: In Fig.~\ref{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTj1}, we show the $p_T$ distribution of $j_1$.
836: The Jacobian peak at $p_T \sim \MWR/2 \sim 1.5\TeV$ is clearly visible,
837: but is noticeably broader for $t$ and $q$ jets than $N$ jets.
838: 
839: With respect to LO+PS, quark jets possess a varying differential $K$-Factor that falls below $\confirm{1}$ for $p_T\lesssim1\TeV$,
840: and grows to $K_{p_T}^{\rm NLOPS}\sim1.2$ for larger $p_T$.
841: For neutrino jets, $K_{p_T}^{\rm NLOPS}\approx 1.2$ and is approximately constant across all $p_T$.
842: Numerically, $K_{p_T}^{\rm NLOPS}\approx 1.2$ is very close to the total inclusive NLO $K$-factor for $\WR$ production, 
843: which is driven by virtual and soft corrections.
844: 
845: We attribute the differences in broadening and $K_{p_T}^{\rm NLOPS}$ simply to the fact that quarks carry net color charge, unlike neutrinos:
846: 
847: Quark jets are susceptible to hard, wide-angle FSR that carry away momentum and causes broadening in the $p_T$ spectrum.
848: In DY-type processes, this is more accurately modeled by matrix element corrections that first appear at NLO in QCD than by parton showers.
849: 
850: 
851: In Fig.~\ref{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_yj1} is the rapidity $(y)$ distribution of $j_1$.
852: Compared to quark jets, heavy neutrino jets possesses a broader, flatter distribution.
853: With respect to LO+PS, again, $K_{p_T}^{\rm NLOPS}\approx 1.2$ and is approximately constant for neutrino jets.
854: For quarks jets, we observe a depletion of events with larger rapidities, and is consistent with the $p_T$ spectrum at NLO+PS.
855: 
856: 
857: 
858: We show in Fig.~\ref{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1} the jet mass distribution centered about $m_t$.
859: For heavy neutrino and top jets, the resonant peak around $m_t$ is unambiguous.
860: As the light quark jet contribution is a continuum at this mass scale, it is featureless.
861: 
862: Most striking is the upward shift in the top jet mass compared to the neutrino jet mass.
863: The shift is caused, in part, by the production of an off-shell top that then emits a (semi-)collinear radiation and is brought on-shell.
864: The collinear nature of the emission means it is captured by the sequential jet algorithm and is well-modeled by parton showers.
865: As $\MWR\gg m_t$, such a configuration is not phase space suppressed.
866: Non-perturbative and large finite width effects are also important\cite{Skands:2007zg,Hoang:2008xm}.
867: For more details, see, e.g., \cite{Skands:2007zg,Hoang:2008xm} and references therein.
868: 
869: However, as neutrinos are not subject to such effects, $N$ jets retains their narrow, resonant structure, even after showering and hadronization.
870: This suggests that searches for neutrino jets, as proposed by~\cite{Ferrari:2000sp,Mitra:2016kov},
871: may be able to impose much more aggressive invariant mass cuts than the 15 GeV presently used in LHC top quark mass studies~\cite{Aad:2015waa}.
872: 
873: 
874: 
875: In Fig.~\ref{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_mj1Hemi1} we plot the ratio of $m_{j_1}/M_{\rm Hemisphere}$,
876: where $M_{\rm Hemisphere}$ is the hemisphere mass associated with $j_1$.
877: We define the hemisphere mass of the leading jet simply as the invariant mass of all jet momenta $p_k$ in the same hemisphere as $j_1$, i.e.,
878: \begin{equation}
879:  M_{\rm Hemisphere} = \sqrt{p_{\rm Hemisphere}^2},	\quad\text{where}\quad
880:  p_{\rm Hemisphere} = \sum_{k\in\{jets\}} p_k 		\quad\text{and}\quad
881:  \hat{p}_k\cdot\hat{p}_{j_1} > 1.
882:  \label{eq:mHemiDef}
883: \end{equation}
884: Due to the large $\WR$ mass we consider, it is largely at rest in $\sqrt{s}=13\TeV$ collisions.
885: This is supported by Fig.~\ref{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTWRreco}.
886: Subsequently, while not rigorously infrared-collinear safe, 
887: the axis defined by the direction of hardest jet is the thrust axis to a good approximation, justifying the use of Eq.~(\ref{eq:mHemiDef}).
888: 
889: The utility of this ratio is its sensitivity to radiation associated with a parton but missed by a jet algorithm because the emission angle is too wide,
890: e.g., high-$p_T$, wide angle FSR off a top quark that falls outside the top jet's radius.
891: 
892: Due to the presence of non-global logarithms and jet substructure, as well as parton shower dependence,
893: a complete and systematic study of hemisphere variables is outside the narrow scope of this report.
894: For further details, see~\cite{Dasgupta:2001sh,Banfi:2006gy,Banfi:2010pa,Fischer:2014bja} and references therein.
895: 
896: In the context of the C/A algorithm, the ratio can be interpreted as the mass ratio of a jet with $R=1$ to that of a ``larger'' jet with $R\approx\pi/2$.
897: 
898: In all three channels, we find a sizable fraction of events are concentrated at $0.9 < m_{j_1}/M_{\rm Hemisphere} < 1$,
899: indicating that single the hardest jet from high-mass $\WR$ decays contains most all the radiation one one side of the detector.
900: As expected, fewer quark jet events satisfy this property.
901: 
902: The accumulation at smaller ratios is due to the large contamination from ISR, which is supported by the flat $N$ jet differential $K$-factor.
903: 
904: \begin{figure}[!t]
905: \begin{center}
906: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTWRreco.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_pTWRreco}	}
907: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_yWRreco.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_yWRreco}	}
908: \\
909: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_MWRreco.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_MWRreco}	}
910: \subfigure[]{\includegraphics[scale=1,width=.48\textwidth]{effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_cosThStar.eps}	\label{fig:effLRSMnlo_pp_wr_Xjet_cosThStar}	}
911: \end{center}
912: \caption{
913: Kinematic distributions of the reconstructed $\WR$ system of with respect to 
914: (a) $p_T^{\WRreco}$, 
915: (b) $y^{\WRreco}$, 
916: (c) $M^{\ Reco.}_{\WR}$, and 
917: (d) the polar distribution of $j_1$ in the $\WRreco$'s rest frame for the same configuration as Fig.~\ref{fig:lhcKinematics}.
918: No $m_{j_1}$ cut applied. Lower: NLO+PS-to-LO+PS ratio.
919: } 
920: \label{fig:lhcWRKin}
921: \end{figure}
922: 
923: 
924: In Fig.~\ref{fig:lhcWRKin} we show the kinematics of the reconstructed $\WR$ system built from 
925: the $(j_1 j_2)$ and $(\ell^\pm j)$ systems for the quark and neutrino channels, respectively.
926: No jet mass cuts are applied.
927: 
928: In (a), (b), (c), and (d), we show respectively, $p_T^{\WRreco}$, $y^{\WRreco}$, $M^{\ Reco.}_{\WR}$, and the 
929: polar distribution of $j_1$ in the $\WRreco$'s rest frame.
930: 
931: Due to bin resolution, the Sudakov shoulder in the $p_T$ spectrum is not shown.
932: 
933: In the invariant mass distribution, we find sizable broadening in the quark channels of the $\WR$ mass peak due to hard, wide-angle FSR;
934: this is largely absent for neutrinos.
935: 
936: 
937: Categorically, we observe that neutrino jets possess largely constant differential $K$-factors.
938: This is qualitatively different from quark jets, which feature more dynamical $K_{\mathcal{O}}$.
939: 
940: The result follows from the color-singlet nature of the $pp\rightarrow \WR^\pm \rightarrow Ne^\pm$ process
941: and large mass (in comparison to the total beam c.m.~energy) of the intermediate $\WR$:
942: 
943: Since $N$ and $e$ are color neutral, they do not undergo QCD FSR, implying that all QCD corrections 
944: are confined to the $q\overline{q'}\rightarrow \WR^{*}$ subprocess.
945: However, due to the large $\MWR$ considered, high-$p_T$ ISR is phase space-suppressed, leaving only hard-collinear (HC) and soft ISR.
946: 
947: HC radiation is encapsulated in the definitions of PDFs and parton showers, and therefore is the same at LO and NLO.
948: 
949: For high-mass DY processes, in both the SM and generic BSM scenarios,
950: virtual corrections and soft radiation amplitudes factorize into the Born amplitude and universal form factors that 
951: combine (due to the KLN theorem) into a finite QCD scaling factor.
952: 
953: Subsequently, total and differential NLO in QCD $K$-factors for high-mass DY systems are constant, up to running of $\alpha_s(\mu)$.
954: 
955: 
956: 
957: 
958: 
959: \section{Summary and Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
960: The LRSM is a predictive and economic extension of the SM 
961: that explains several observations not accommodated by the SM.
962: 
963: It postulates the existence of the $\WR,\ZR,$ gauge bosons and Majorana neutrinos $N$, 
964: that may be discovered/studied at the LHC or near-future collider experiment.
965: 
966: We report the construction of a new MC model file capable of simulating fully differential benchmark 
967: $\WR,\ZR,$ and $N$ production and decay processes at an accuracy up to NLO+PS using the FR+\mgamc+PY8 framework. 
968: 
969: Such corrections are necessary to realistically model QCD radiation at hadron super colliders.
970: 
971: Remarkably fewer input parameters are required in comparison to LO LRSM implementations.
972:

703: LHiggs := Block[{ii,mu, feynmangaugerules},
704:   feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
705:  
706:   ExpandIndices[DC[Phibar[ii],mu] DC[Phi[ii],mu] + muH^2 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] - lam Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] Phibar[jj] Phi[jj], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]/.feynmangaugerules

710:   feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
711:  
712:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
713:    -yd[ff2, ff3] CKM[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].dR [sp, ff3, cc] Phi[ii] - 
714:     yl[ff1, ff3] LLbar[sp, ii, ff1].lR [sp, ff3] Phi[ii] - 
715:     yu[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].uR [sp, ff2, cc] Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj], FlavorExpand -> SU2D];

720: LGhost := Block[{LGh1,LGhw,LGhs,LGhphi,mu, generators,gh,ghbar,Vectorize,phi1,phi2,togoldstones,doublet,doublet0},
721:   (* Pure gauge piece *) 	
722:   LGh1 = -ghBbar.del[DC[ghB,mu],mu];
723:   LGhw = -ghWibar[ii].del[DC[ghWi[ii],mu],mu];
724:   LGhs = -ghGbar[ii].del[DC[ghG[ii],mu],mu];
725: 
726:   (* Scalar pieces: see Peskin pages 739-742 *)
727:   (* phi1 and phi2 are the real degrees of freedom of GP *)
728:   (* Vectorize transforms a doublet in a vector in the phi-basis, i.e. the basis of real degrees of freedom *)
729:   gh    = {ghB, ghWi[1], ghWi[2], ghWi[3]};
730:   ghbar = {ghBbar, ghWibar[1], ghWibar[2], ghWibar[3]};
731:   generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};
732:   doublet = Expand[{(-I phi1 - phi2)/Sqrt[2], Phi[2]} /. MR$Definitions /. vev -> 0];

    InteractionOrder -> {QED, 1},
    ParameterName    -> {yl[1,1] -> ye, yl[2,2] -> ym, yl[3,3] -> ytau},
    TeX              -> Superscript[y, l],
    Description      -> "Lepton Yukawa couplings"
  },
  yu == {
    ParameterType    -> Internal,
    Indices          -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Definitions      -> {yu[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> 0  /; (i =!= j)},
    Value            -> {yu[1,1] -> Sqrt[2] ymup/vev, yu[2,2] -> Sqrt[2] ymc/vev, yu[3,3] -> Sqrt[2] ymt/vev},
    InteractionOrder -> {QED, 1},
    ParameterName    -> {yu[1,1] -> yup, yu[2,2] -> yc, yu[3,3] -> yt},
    TeX              -> Superscript[y, u],
    Description      -> "Up-type Yukawa couplings"
  },
  yd == {
    ParameterType    -> Internal,
    Indices          -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Definitions      -> {yd[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> 0  /; (i =!= j)},
    Value            -> {yd[1,1] -> Sqrt[2] ymdo/vev, yd[2,2] -> Sqrt[2] yms/vev, yd[3,3] -> Sqrt[2] ymb/vev},
    InteractionOrder -> {QED, 1},
    ParameterName    -> {yd[1,1] -> ydo, yd[2,2] -> ys, yd[3,3] -> yb},
    TeX              -> Superscript[y, d],
    Description      -> "Down-type Yukawa couplings"
  },
(* N. B. : only Cabibbo mixing! *)
  CKM == { 
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {CKM[1,1] -> Cos[cabi],  CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi], CKM[1,3] -> 0,
                      CKM[2,1] -> -Sin[cabi], CKM[2,2] -> Cos[cabi], CKM[2,3] -> 0,
                      CKM[3,1] -> 0,          CKM[3,2] -> 0,         CKM[3,3] -> 1},
    TeX         -> Superscript[V,CKM],
    Description -> "CKM-Matrix"}
};

(* ************************** *)
(* *****   Lagrangian   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

LGauge := Block[{mu,nu,ii,aa}, 
  ExpandIndices[-1/4 FS[B,mu,nu] FS[B,mu,nu] - 1/4 FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] - 1/4 FS[G,mu,nu,aa] FS[G,mu,nu,aa], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];

LFermions := Block[{mu}, 
  ExpandIndices[I*(
    QLbar.Ga[mu].DC[QL, mu] + LLbar.Ga[mu].DC[LL, mu] + uRbar.Ga[mu].DC[uR, mu] + dRbar.Ga[mu].DC[dR, mu] + lRbar.Ga[mu].DC[lR, mu]), 
  FlavorExpand->{SU2W,SU2D}]/.{CKM[a_,b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_,c_]]->IndexDelta[b,c], CKM[b_,a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_,a_]]->IndexDelta[b,c]}];

LHiggs := Block[{ii,mu, feynmangaugerules},
  feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
 
  ExpandIndices[DC[Phibar[ii],mu] DC[Phi[ii],mu] + muH^2 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] - lam Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] Phibar[jj] Phi[jj], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]/.feynmangaugerules
 ];

LYukawa := Block[{sp,ii,jj,cc,ff1,ff2,ff3,yuk,feynmangaugerules},
  feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
 
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
   -yd[ff2, ff3] CKM[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].dR [sp, ff3, cc] Phi[ii] - 
    yl[ff1, ff3] LLbar[sp, ii, ff1].lR [sp, ff3] Phi[ii] - 
    yu[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].uR [sp, ff2, cc] Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj], FlavorExpand -> SU2D];
  yuk = yuk /. { CKM[a_, b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_, c_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c], CKM[b_, a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_, a_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c]};
  yuk+HC[yuk]/.feynmangaugerules
 ];

LGhost := Block[{LGh1,LGhw,LGhs,LGhphi,mu, generators,gh,ghbar,Vectorize,phi1,phi2,togoldstones,doublet,doublet0},
  (* Pure gauge piece *) 	
  LGh1 = -ghBbar.del[DC[ghB,mu],mu];
  LGhw = -ghWibar[ii].del[DC[ghWi[ii],mu],mu];
  LGhs = -ghGbar[ii].del[DC[ghG[ii],mu],mu];

  (* Scalar pieces: see Peskin pages 739-742 *)
  (* phi1 and phi2 are the real degrees of freedom of GP *)
  (* Vectorize transforms a doublet in a vector in the phi-basis, i.e. the basis of real degrees of freedom *)
  gh    = {ghB, ghWi[1], ghWi[2], ghWi[3]};
  ghbar = {ghBbar, ghWibar[1], ghWibar[2], ghWibar[3]};
  generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};
  doublet = Expand[{(-I phi1 - phi2)/Sqrt[2], Phi[2]} /. MR$Definitions /. vev -> 0]; 
  doublet0 = {0, vev/Sqrt[2]};
  Vectorize[{a_, b_}]:= Simplify[{Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[b]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[b]]}/.{Im[_]->0, Re[num_]->num}];
  togoldstones := {phi1 -> (GP + GPbar)/Sqrt[2], phi2 -> (-GP + GPbar)/(I Sqrt[2])};
  LGhphi=Plus@@Flatten[Table[-ghbar[[kkk]].gh[[lll]] Vectorize[generators[[kkk]].doublet0].Vectorize[generators[[lll]].(doublet+doublet0)],{kkk,4},{lll,4}]] /.togoldstones;

ExpandIndices[ LGhs + If[FeynmanGauge, LGh1 + LGhw + LGhphi,0], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];

LSM:= LGauge + LFermions + LHiggs + LYukawa + LGhost;

973: Publicly available UFO files~\cite{nloFRModel} are compatible with similar general-purpose event generators, e.g., 
974: HERWIG and SHERPA.
975: 
976: Our NLO in QCD corrections and residual scale uncertainty for inclusive $pp\rightarrow\WR,\ZR$ production at the 13 TeV LHC and 100 TeV VLHC 
977: are in agreement with other findings.
978: 
979: This is similarly the case for inclusive $e^-p\rightarrow N+X$ production at a future LHeC experiment.
980: 
981: 
982: As a case study, we have investigated at NLO+PS accuracy,
983: the kinematics of heavy neutrino jets and top jets originating from the decay of high-mass $\WR$ decays at the 13 TeV LHC.
984: 
985: With respect to LO+PS, we find \confirm{appreciable} changes to top jet kinematics that we attribute hard, wide-angle FSR not captured by parton showers.
986: 
987: Conversely, due to the absence of such FSR, we find neutrino jets kinematics are resilient against the effects of parton showers and hadronization.
988: This suggests that in searches for neutrino jets, 
989: aggressive selection cuts that would otherwise be inappropriate for top jets can be imposed with minimal signal loss.

1017: \section{EffLRSM@NLO Signal Simulation with \mgamc}\label{app:sigDef}
1018: In this section, we provide brief instructions for simulating particle production in the Effective LRSM using the MG5\_aMC@NLO+PY8 framework
1019: for FO and PS predictions.
1020: 
1021: The inclusive $pp\rightarrow\WR$ cross section at NLO can be calculated for $\MWR\in[1\TeV,6\TeV]$ in 1 TeV increments
1022: with the scale choice of Eq.~(\ref{eq:mgScale}) via the \mgamc~commands:
1023: \begin{verbatim}
1024: > import model EffLRSM_NLO
1025: > define p  = u c d s b u~ c~ d~ s~ b~ g
1026: > define j  = p
1027: > define wr = wr+ wr-
1028: > generate p p > wr [QCD]
1029: > output PP_WR_NLO; launch
1030: > order=NLO 
1031: > fixed_order=ON
1032: > set MWR scan:range(1000,6001,1000)
1033: > set dynamical_scale_choice 3
1034: \end{verbatim}
1035: In the same environment, the LO cross section at, say, 100 TeV can be computed with the following:
1036: \begin{verbatim}
1037: > launch PP_WR_NLO
1038: > order=LO
1039: > set LHC 100
1040: \end{verbatim}
1041: Inclusive $pp\rightarrow\ZR$ production rates are obtained by making the obvious \texttt{wr}$~\rightarrow~$\texttt{zr} substitution.
1042: 
1043: To simulate $pp\rightarrow \WR \rightarrow Ne^\pm$ at NLO+PS with finite $\WR$ width effects, the commands are:
1044: \begin{verbatim}
1045: > generate p p > wr+ > n1 e+ [QCD]
1046: > add process p p > wr- > n1 e- [QCD]
1047: > output PP_WR_Ne_NLO; launch
1048: \end{verbatim}
1049: Other leptons, e.g., $N_2$ or $\tau^\pm$, can appear in the final state but may require regeneration of the LRSM UFO;
1050: default lepton mixing is set according to Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}).
1051: For $\WR^*\rightarrow tb$, the commands are:
1052: \begin{verbatim}
1053: > generate p p > wr+ > t b~ [QCD]
1054: > add process p p > wr- > t~ b [QCD]
1055: > output PP_WR_tb_NLO; launch
1056: \end{verbatim}
1057: 
1058: Simulating inclusive $e^-p\rightarrow N+X$ production at LO for $\MWR=3\TeV$ and $\mN\in[100\GeV,1\TeV]$ in 100 GeV increments 
1059: can be done using the following:
1060: \begin{verbatim}
1061: > generate generate e- p > n1 j
1062: > output PP_ep_NX_LO; launch
1063: > set lpp1 0
1064: > set ebeam1 140
1065: > set ebeam2 7000
1066: > set polbeam1 80
1067: > set MWR 3000
1068: > set mn1 scan:range(100,1001,100)
1069: \end{verbatim}
1070: The third line turns off the PDF for the electron beam, whereas the fourth and fifth line sets the individual beam energies.
1071: The line after sets the electron beam polarization to $P_e = +80\%$.
1072: 
1073: \section{Three-Body Decays of $N$ and $t$ in MadSpin}\label{app:MadSpin}
1074: As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:Decay}, decays of the lightest heavy neutrino in the LRSM 
1075: are dominated by the process $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm W^{\mp *}_R \rightarrow \ell^\pm q \overline{q'}$. 
1076: Here $\WR$ is far off-shell.
1077: To model such processes using MadSpin within the \mgamc framework requires adding to \texttt{Cards/madspin\_card.dat} the following:
1078: \begin{verbatim}
1079: set spinmode onshell 
1080: define  q = u c d s u~ c~ d~ s~ 
1081: define ee = e+ e- 
1082: decay  n1 > ee q q
1083: launch
1084: \end{verbatim}
1085: For top quarks decaying to hadronic and leptonic final states, we use the following MadSpin syntax:
1086: \begin{verbatim}
1087: decay t  > w+ b,  w+ > all all
1088: decay t~ > w- b~, w- > all all
1089: launch
1090: \end{verbatim}
1091: In both cases, we retain full spin correlation with the hard process matrix elements.
1092: 
1093: 
1094: 
1095: \section{User Defined Generator-Level Cuts in \mgamc}\label{app:GenCuts}
1096: Imposing phase space cuts on final-state top quarks and heavy neutrinos in~\mgamc~
1097: requires modifying the file \texttt{SubProcesses/cuts.f} in the local process directory, i.e.,
1098: the directory \texttt{PP\_WR\_Ne\_NLO} or \texttt{PP\_WR\_tb\_NLO} if following App.~\ref{app:sigDef}.
1099: To apply out generator-level cut of $p_T > 750\GeV$ with NLO in QCD accuracy,
1100: we insert after Line 377 of \texttt{cuts.f} the following:
1101: \begin{verbatim}
1102: do i=1,nexternal                ! loop over all external particles
1103:     if (istatus(i).eq.1  .and.  ! check if final-state particle and
1104:   &  (abs(ipdg(i)).eq.6 .or.    ! PID == top quark or
1105:   &   abs(ipdg(i)).eq.9900012)  ! PID == heavy neutrino
1106:   &    ) then    
1107: C Reject event if pT < 750 GeV
1108:             if ( p(1,i)**2+p(2,i)**2 .lt. (750.0d0)**2 ) then
1109:                passcuts_user=.false.
1110:                return
1111:             endif
1112:     endif
1113: enddo
1114: \end{verbatim}

Our NLO in QCD corrections and residual scale uncertainty for inclusive $pp\rightarrow\WR,\ZR$ production at the 13 TeV LHC and 100 TeV VLHC 
are in agreement with other findings.

This is similarly the case for inclusive $e^-p\rightarrow N+X$ production at a future LHeC experiment.


As a case study, we have investigated at NLO+PS accuracy,
the kinematics of heavy neutrino jets and top jets originating from the decay of high-mass $\WR$ decays at the 13 TeV LHC.

With respect to LO+PS, we find \confirm{appreciable} changes to top jet kinematics that we attribute hard, wide-angle FSR not captured by parton showers.

Conversely, due to the absence of such FSR, we find neutrino jets kinematics are resilient against the effects of parton showers and hadronization.
This suggests that in searches for neutrino jets, 
aggressive selection cuts that would otherwise be inappropriate for top jets can be imposed with minimal signal loss.

\section{EffLRSM@NLO Signal Simulation with \mgamc}\label{app:sigDef}
In this section, we provide brief instructions for simulating particle production in the Effective LRSM using the MG5\_aMC@NLO+PY8 framework
for FO and PS predictions.

The inclusive $pp\rightarrow\WR$ cross section at NLO can be calculated for $\MWR\in[1\TeV,6\TeV]$ in 1 TeV increments
with the scale choice of Eq.~(\ref{eq:mgScale}) via the \mgamc~commands:
\begin{verbatim}
> import model EffLRSM_NLO
> define p  = u c d s b u~ c~ d~ s~ b~ g
> define j  = p
> define wr = wr+ wr-
> generate p p > wr [QCD]
> output PP_WR_NLO; launch
> order=NLO 
> fixed_order=ON
> set MWR scan:range(1000,6001,1000)
> set dynamical_scale_choice 3
\end{verbatim}
In the same environment, the LO cross section at, say, 100 TeV can be computed with the following:
\begin{verbatim}
> launch PP_WR_NLO
> order=LO
> set LHC 100
\end{verbatim}
Inclusive $pp\rightarrow\ZR$ production rates are obtained by making the obvious \texttt{wr}$~\rightarrow~$\texttt{zr} substitution.

To simulate $pp\rightarrow \WR \rightarrow Ne^\pm$ at NLO+PS with finite $\WR$ width effects, the commands are:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate p p > wr+ > n1 e+ [QCD]
> add process p p > wr- > n1 e- [QCD]
> output PP_WR_Ne_NLO; launch
\end{verbatim}
Other leptons, e.g., $N_2$ or $\tau^\pm$, can appear in the final state but may require regeneration of the LRSM UFO;
default lepton mixing is set according to Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}).
For $\WR^*\rightarrow tb$, the commands are:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate p p > wr+ > t b~ [QCD]
> add process p p > wr- > t~ b [QCD]
> output PP_WR_tb_NLO; launch
\end{verbatim}

Simulating inclusive $e^-p\rightarrow N+X$ production at LO for $\MWR=3\TeV$ and $\mN\in[100\GeV,1\TeV]$ in 100 GeV increments 
can be done using the following:
\begin{verbatim}
> generate generate e- p > n1 j
> output PP_ep_NX_LO; launch
> set lpp1 0
> set ebeam1 140
> set ebeam2 7000
> set polbeam1 80
> set MWR 3000
> set mn1 scan:range(100,1001,100)
\end{verbatim}
The third line turns off the PDF for the electron beam, whereas the fourth and fifth line sets the individual beam energies.
The line after sets the electron beam polarization to $P_e = +80\%$.

\section{Three-Body Decays of $N$ and $t$ in MadSpin}\label{app:MadSpin}
As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:Decay}, decays of the lightest heavy neutrino in the LRSM 
are dominated by the process $N\rightarrow \ell^\pm W^{\mp *}_R \rightarrow \ell^\pm q \overline{q'}$. 
Here $\WR$ is far off-shell.
To model such processes using MadSpin within the \mgamc framework requires adding to \texttt{Cards/madspin\_card.dat} the following:
\begin{verbatim}
set spinmode onshell 
define  q = u c d s u~ c~ d~ s~ 
define ee = e+ e- 
decay  n1 > ee q q
launch
\end{verbatim}
For top quarks decaying to hadronic and leptonic final states, we use the following MadSpin syntax:
\begin{verbatim}
decay t  > w+ b,  w+ > all all
decay t~ > w- b~, w- > all all
launch
\end{verbatim}
In both cases, we retain full spin correlation with the hard process matrix elements.



\section{User Defined Generator-Level Cuts in \mgamc}\label{app:GenCuts}
Imposing phase space cuts on final-state top quarks and heavy neutrinos in~\mgamc~
requires modifying the file \texttt{SubProcesses/cuts.f} in the local process directory, i.e.,
the directory \texttt{PP\_WR\_Ne\_NLO} or \texttt{PP\_WR\_tb\_NLO} if following App.~\ref{app:sigDef}.
To apply out generator-level cut of $p_T > 750\GeV$ with NLO in QCD accuracy,
we insert after Line 377 of \texttt{cuts.f} the following:
\begin{verbatim}
do i=1,nexternal                ! loop over all external particles
    if (istatus(i).eq.1  .and.  ! check if final-state particle and
  &  (abs(ipdg(i)).eq.6 .or.    ! PID == top quark or
  &   abs(ipdg(i)).eq.9900012)  ! PID == heavy neutrino
  &    ) then    
C Reject event if pT < 750 GeV
            if ( p(1,i)**2+p(2,i)**2 .lt. (750.0d0)**2 ) then
               passcuts_user=.false.
               return
            endif
    endif
enddo
\end{verbatim}

(*****************************************************************************************)
(******  Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model (EffLRSM) add-on on top of SM.fr       ******)
(******  Extracted from arXiv:1610.08985 (Mattelaer, Mitra, Ruiz)                     ******)
(******  New content: W_R^+-, Z_R gauge bosons and three heavy Majorana neutrinos N_i  ******)
(*****************************************************************************************)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****  Information   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

M$ModelName = "EffLRSM_gen";

M$Information = {
  Authors      -> {"O. Mattelaer", "M. Mitra", "R. Ruiz"},
  Version      -> "1.0.0",
  Date         -> "27. 10. 2016",
  Institutions -> {"CP3, Universite catholique de Louvain", "IISER Mohali", "IPPP, Durham University"},
  Emails       -> {"olivier.mattelaer@uclouvain.be", "manimala@iisermohali.ac.in", "richard.ruiz@durham.ac.uk"},
  References   -> "arXiv:1610.08985"
};

(* ************************** *)
(* ***** Interaction orders *****)
(* ************************** *)

M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {
  {QCD, 1},
  {QED, 2},
  {NP, 1}
};

(* ************************** *)
(* *****      Indices     *****)
(* ************************** *)

(* No new indices: Colour, Gluon, Generation, SU2D and SU2W are all declared by SM.fr.
   No non-fundamental colour representation occurs: every new particle is a colour
   singlet, hence no IndexRange declaration and no AddGaugeRepresentation line. *)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****   Parameters   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

M$Parameters = {

  (* External parameters *)
  kappaRq == {
    ParameterType    -> External,
    BlockName        -> LRSMINPUTS,
    OrderBlock       -> 1,
    Value            -> 1.,
    InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1},
    Description      -> "kappa_R^q : W_R/Z_R coupling normalisation for quarks (Eqs. 2,7)"
  },
  kappaRl == {
    ParameterType    -> External,
    BlockName        -> LRSMINPUTS,
    OrderBlock       -> 2,
    Value            -> 1.,
    InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1},
    Description      -> "kappa_R^l : W_R/Z_R coupling normalisation for leptons (Eqs. 3,7)"
  },

  (* Internal parameters *)
  VCKMR == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {VCKMR[1,1] -> 1,  VCKMR[1,2] -> 0,  VCKMR[1,3] -> 0,
                      VCKMR[2,1] -> 0,  VCKMR[2,2] -> 1,  VCKMR[2,3] -> 0,
                      VCKMR[3,1] -> 0,  VCKMR[3,2] -> 0,  VCKMR[3,3] -> 1},
    Description   -> "Right-handed CKM matrix V^{CKM'} (Eq. 2): diagonal with unit entries (Sec. 2)"
  },
  YN == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {YN[1,1] -> 1,  YN[1,2] -> 0,  YN[1,3] -> 0,
                      YN[2,1] -> 0,  YN[2,2] -> 1,  YN[2,3] -> 0,
                      YN[3,1] -> 0,  YN[3,2] -> 0,  YN[3,3] -> 1},
    Description   -> "W_R leptonic mixing Y_{l m'} (Eq. 5): |Y_eN1|=|Y_muN2|=|Y_tauN3|=1, all others 0"
  },
  tw2 == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Value         -> sw2/cw2,
    Description   -> "tan^2(theta_W) = sin^2(theta_W)/cos^2(theta_W)"
  }
};

(* ************************** *)
(* ***** Particle classes *****)
(* ************************** *)

M$ClassesDescription = {

  (* Right-handed charged gauge boson W_R^+ / W_R^- *)
  V[100] == {
    ClassName        -> Wp,
    SelfConjugate    -> False,
    QuantumNumbers   -> {Q -> 1},
    Mass             -> {MWR, 3000.},
    Width            -> {WWr, 84.3},
    ParticleName     -> "wr+",
    AntiParticleName -> "wr-",
    PDG              -> 9900024,
    PropagatorLabel  -> "wr",
    PropagatorType   -> Sine,
    PropagatorArrow  -> Forward,
    FullName         -> "W_R"
  },

  (* Right-handed neutral gauge boson Z_R *)
  V[101] == {
    ClassName       -> Zr,
    SelfConjugate   -> True,
    Mass            -> {MZR, 5070.},
    Width           -> {WZr, 114.},
    ParticleName    -> "zr",
    PDG             -> 9900023,
    PropagatorLabel -> "zr",
    PropagatorType  -> Sine,
    PropagatorArrow -> None,
    FullName        -> "Z_R"
  },

  (* Heavy Majorana neutrinos N_1, N_2, N_3 *)
  F[100] == {
    ClassName       -> NR,
    ClassMembers    -> {N1, N2, N3},
    Indices         -> {Index[Generation]},
    FlavorIndex     -> Generation,
    SelfConjugate   -> True,
    Mass            -> {MN, {MN1, 173.3}, {MN2, 1.*^12}, {MN3, 1.*^12}},
    Width           -> {{WN1, 2.12*^-8}, {WN2, 0}, {WN3, 0}},
    PropagatorLabel -> {"N", "N1", "N2", "N3"},
    PropagatorType  -> Straight,
    PropagatorArrow -> None,
    PDG             -> {9900012, 9900014, 9900016},
    ParticleName    -> {"n1", "n2", "n3"},
    FullName        -> {"Heavy neutrino 1", "Heavy neutrino 2", "Heavy neutrino 3"}
  }
};

GaugeXi[ V[100] ] = GaugeXi[Wp];
GaugeXi[ V[101] ] = GaugeXi[Zr];

(* ************************** *)
(* *****    Lagrangian   *****)
(* ************************** *)

(* Free-field term for W_R^+- (complex vector, task rule 1) *)
LWpkin := Block[{mu, nu},
  ExpandIndices[-1/2 FS[Wpbar, mu, nu] FS[Wp, mu, nu] + MWR^2 Wpbar[mu] Wp[mu]]
];

(* Free-field term for Z_R (real vector, task rule 1) *)
LZrkin := Block[{mu, nu},
  ExpandIndices[-1/4 FS[Zr, mu, nu] FS[Zr, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZR^2 Zr[mu] Zr[mu]]
];

(* Free-field term for the heavy Majorana neutrinos (task rules 1, 15) *)
LNRkin := Block[{mu},
  ExpandIndices[I/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].del[NR, mu]] -
    1/2 MN1 NRbar[1].NR[1] - 1/2 MN2 NRbar[2].NR[2] - 1/2 MN3 NRbar[3].NR[3]
];

(* Eq. (2): W_R charged current to quarks + H.c. *)
LWRqq := Block[{mu, hq},
  hq = ExpandIndices[(-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[2]) uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq Wp[mu]];
  hq + HC[hq]
];

(* Eq. (3): W_R charged current to leptons + H.c.
   The X_lm nu^c term is dropped because the benchmark sets X_lm = 0 (Eq. (5)). *)
LWRlnu := Block[{mu, hl},
  hl = ExpandIndices[(-kappaRl gw/Sqrt[2]) NRbar.YN.Ga[mu].ProjP.l Wp[mu]];
  hl + HC[hl]
];

(* Eqs. (7)-(9): Z_R neutral currents.
   Overall prefactor -kappa g/Sqrt[1 - tan^2(th_W)/kappa^2] (Sqrt in the denominator,
   read literally from the LaTeX) times g_L/g_R of Eqs. (8)-(9).
   Real coefficients => Hermitian as written; the paper adds no H.c., so none is added. *)
LZRff := Block[{mu},
  ExpandIndices[
    (-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[1 - tw2/kappaRq^2]) (
      (-tw2/(6 kappaRq^2)) uqbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.uq
    + (1/2 - 2 tw2/(3 kappaRq^2)) uqbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.uq
    + (-tw2/(6 kappaRq^2)) dqbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq
    + (-1/2 + tw2/(3 kappaRq^2)) dqbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.dq
    )
  + (-kappaRl gw/Sqrt[1 - tw2/kappaRl^2]) (
      (tw2/(2 kappaRl^2)) lbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.l
    + (-1/2 + tw2/kappaRl^2) lbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.l
    + (tw2/(2 kappaRl^2)) vlbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.vl
    + 1/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.NR
    )
  ] Zr[mu]
];

LTotal := LWpkin + LZrkin + LNRkin + LWRqq + LWRlnu + LZRff;

## Important Details

No new scalars (paper limitation), no other states (B/X combine into SM hypercharge).
- Parameters: External `kappaRq` (BlockName LRSMINPUTS, OrderBlock 1, Value 1., {NP,1}), `kappaRl` (OrderBlock 2, 1., {NP,1}); Internal matrices `VCKMR` and `YN` (Unitary->True, explicit identity component values — paper says mixing changes require UFO regeneration ⇒ Internal, SM CKM-style, no InteractionOrder, like SM's `CKM`); Internal `tw2 -> sw2/cw2`. Masses/widths via class declarations: MWR 3000., WWr 84.3, MZR 5070., WZr 114., MN {MN1 173.3, MN2/MN3 1.*^12}, WN {WN1 2.12*^-8, WN2/WN3 0}.

- Chirality: ProjP = P_R, ProjM = P_L (confirmed from SM `lR:>ProjP`, `LL:>ProjM`).
- Fraction placements (rule 7, cross-checked): W_R currents `-kappa g/Sqrt[2]` (LaTeX line 281, 293-298; verified vs Γ(W→qq')=N_c κ²g²M/(48π) reproducing Table II 8.4 GeV/flavour, 50.7, 84.3); Z_R prefactor `-kappa g/Sqrt[1 - tw2/kappa^2]` with Sqrt in denominator (LaTeX line 352; verified vs Γ(Z→ff) formula and Table II: tt̄ 11.3, ℓℓ 3×2.56=7.64, qq 82.3, νν 3×0.93=2.78, N1N1 10.2, total 114); g_L/g_R from LaTeX lines 359-361 (gLu=gLd=-tw2/(6κq²), gRu=1/2-2tw2/(3κq²), gRd=-1/2+tw2/(3κq²), gZeL=gZnL=tw2/(2κl²), gZeR=-1/2+tw2/κl², gRN=1/2) — numerically verified against Table II.
- g_L is equal within each SU(2)_L doublet ⇒ LH currents doublet-universal ⇒ SU(2) invariance holds; RH fields are singlets.
- X_{ℓm} / \overline{ν^c} term dropped (X=0, Eq. 5) ⇒ no CC[] anywhere; N entered as plain Majorana bar (`NRbar`).
- Z_R term: no HC (real-coefficient Hermitian bilinears, paper writes no H.c.); W_R terms include `+ HC[...]` (paper +H.c.).
- No new U(1) declared (no new gauge group; physical fields declare only Q, mirroring SM.fr ⇒ all Y sums trivially 0); no 1/Λ^d operators (all d=4); no mass mixing (paper: W_R/Z_R aligned with mass eigenstates, X=0).
- PDG scheme: 9900024 (wr), 9900023 (zr), {9900012, 9900014, 9900016} (n1-3; 9900012 confirmed from paper's cuts.f); ParticleNames "wr+", "wr-", "zr", "n1","n2","n3" (match paper's MG syntax).
- Only paper, SM.fr, TASK.md were read (rule 6 satisfied: no cached .fr seen).

(*****************************************************************************************)
(******  Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model (EffLRSM) add-on on top of SM.fr       ******)
(******  Extracted from arXiv:1610.08985 (Mattelaer, Mitra, Ruiz)                     ******)
(******  New content: W_R^+-, Z_R gauge bosons and three heavy Majorana neutrinos N_i  ******)
(*****************************************************************************************)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****  Information   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

M$ModelName = "EffLRSM_gen";

M$Information = {
  Authors      -> {"O. Mattelaer", "M. Mitra", "R. Ruiz"},
  Version      -> "1.0.0",
  Date         -> "27. 10. 2016",
  Institutions -> {"CP3, Universite catholique de Louvain", "IISER Mohali", "IPPP, Durham University"},
  Emails       -> {"olivier.mattelaer@uclouvain.be", "manimala@iisermohali.ac.in", "richard.ruiz@durham.ac.uk"},
  References   -> "arXiv:1610.08985"
};

(* ************************** *)
(* ***** Interaction orders *****)
(* ************************** *)

M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {
  {QCD, 1},
  {QED, 2},
  {NP, 1}
};

(* ************************** *)
(* *****      Indices     *****)
(* ************************** *)

(* No new indices: Colour, Gluon, Generation, SU2D and SU2W are all declared by SM.fr.
   No non-fundamental colour representation occurs: every new particle is a colour
   singlet, hence no IndexRange declaration and no AddGaugeRepresentation line. *)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****   Parameters   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

M$Parameters = {

  (* External parameters *)
  kappaRq == {
    ParameterType    -> External,
    BlockName        -> LRSMINPUTS,
    OrderBlock       -> 1,
    Value            -> 1.,
    InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1},
    Description      -> "kappa_R^q : W_R/Z_R coupling normalisation for quarks (Eqs. 2,7)"
  },
  kappaRl == {
    ParameterType    -> External,
    BlockName        -> LRSMINPUTS,
    OrderBlock       -> 2,
    Value            -> 1.,
    InteractionOrder -> {NP, 1},
    Description      -> "kappa_R^l : W_R/Z_R coupling normalisation for leptons (Eqs. 3,7)"
  },

  (* Internal parameters *)
  VCKMR == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {VCKMR[1,1] -> 1,  VCKMR[1,2] -> 0,  VCKMR[1,3] -> 0,
                      VCKMR[2,1] -> 0,  VCKMR[2,2] -> 1,  VCKMR[2,3] -> 0,
                      VCKMR[3,1] -> 0,  VCKMR[3,2] -> 0,  VCKMR[3,3] -> 1},
    Description   -> "Right-handed CKM matrix V^{CKM'} (Eq. 2): diagonal with unit entries (Sec. 2)"
  },
  YN == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {YN[1,1] -> 1,  YN[1,2] -> 0,  YN[1,3] -> 0,
                      YN[2,1] -> 0,  YN[2,2] -> 1,  YN[2,3] -> 0,
                      YN[3,1] -> 0,  YN[3,2] -> 0,  YN[3,3] -> 1},
    Description   -> "W_R leptonic mixing Y_{l m'} (Eq. 5): |Y_eN1|=|Y_muN2|=|Y_tauN3|=1, all others 0"
  },
  tw2 == {
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Value         -> sw2/cw2,
    Description   -> "tan^2(theta_W) = sin^2(theta_W)/cos^2(theta_W)"
  }
};

(* ************************** *)
(* ***** Particle classes *****)
(* ************************** *)

M$ClassesDescription = {

  (* Right-handed charged gauge boson W_R^+ / W_R^- *)
  V[100] == {
    ClassName        -> Wp,
    SelfConjugate    -> False,
    QuantumNumbers   -> {Q -> 1},
    Mass             -> {MWR, 3000.},
    Width            -> {WWr, 84.3},
    ParticleName     -> "wr+",
    AntiParticleName -> "wr-",
    PDG              -> 9900024,
    PropagatorLabel  -> "wr",
    PropagatorType   -> Sine,
    PropagatorArrow  -> Forward,
    FullName         -> "W_R"
  },

  (* Right-handed neutral gauge boson Z_R *)
  V[101] == {
    ClassName       -> Zr,
    SelfConjugate   -> True,
    Mass            -> {MZR, 5070.},
    Width           -> {WZr, 114.},
    ParticleName    -> "zr",
    PDG             -> 9900023,
    PropagatorLabel -> "zr",
    PropagatorType  -> Sine,
    PropagatorArrow -> None,
    FullName        -> "Z_R"
  },

  (* Heavy Majorana neutrinos N_1, N_2, N_3 *)
  F[100] == {
    ClassName       -> NR,
    ClassMembers    -> {N1, N2, N3},
    Indices         -> {Index[Generation]},
    FlavorIndex     -> Generation,
    SelfConjugate   -> True,
    Mass            -> {MN, {MN1, 173.3}, {MN2, 1.*^12}, {MN3, 1.*^12}},
    Width           -> {{WN1, 2.12*^-8}, {WN2, 0}, {WN3, 0}},
    PropagatorLabel -> {"N", "N1", "N2", "N3"},
    PropagatorType  -> Straight,
    PropagatorArrow -> None,
    PDG             -> {9900012, 9900014, 9900016},
    ParticleName    -> {"n1", "n2", "n3"},
    FullName        -> {"Heavy neutrino 1", "Heavy neutrino 2", "Heavy neutrino 3"}
  }
};

GaugeXi[ V[100] ] = GaugeXi[Wp];
GaugeXi[ V[101] ] = GaugeXi[Zr];

(* ************************** *)
(* *****    Lagrangian   *****)
(* ************************** *)

(* Free-field term for W_R^+- (complex vector, task rule 1) *)
LWpkin := Block[{mu, nu},
  ExpandIndices[-1/2 FS[Wpbar, mu, nu] FS[Wp, mu, nu] + MWR^2 Wpbar[mu] Wp[mu]]
];

(* Free-field term for Z_R (real vector, task rule 1) *)
LZrkin := Block[{mu, nu},
  ExpandIndices[-1/4 FS[Zr, mu, nu] FS[Zr, mu, nu] + 1/2 MZR^2 Zr[mu] Zr[mu]]
];

(* Free-field term for the heavy Majorana neutrinos (task rules 1, 15) *)
LNRkin := Block[{mu},
  ExpandIndices[I/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].del[NR, mu]] -
    1/2 MN1 NRbar[1].NR[1] - 1/2 MN2 NRbar[2].NR[2] - 1/2 MN3 NRbar[3].NR[3]
];

(* Eq. (2): W_R charged current to quarks + H.c. *)
LWRqq := Block[{mu, hq},
  hq = ExpandIndices[(-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[2]) uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq Wp[mu]];
  hq + HC[hq]
];

(* Eq. (3): W_R charged current to leptons + H.c.
   The X_lm nu^c term is dropped because the benchmark sets X_lm = 0 (Eq. (5)). *)
LWRlnu := Block[{mu, hl},
  hl = ExpandIndices[(-kappaRl gw/Sqrt[2]) NRbar.YN.Ga[mu].ProjP.l Wp[mu]];
  hl + HC[hl]
];

(* Eqs. (7)-(9): Z_R neutral currents.
   Overall prefactor -kappa g/Sqrt[1 - tan^2(th_W)/kappa^2] (Sqrt in the denominator,
   read literally from the LaTeX) times g_L/g_R of Eqs. (8)-(9).
   Real coefficients => Hermitian as written; the paper adds no H.c., so none is added. *)
LZRff := Block[{mu},
  ExpandIndices[
    (-kappaRq gw/Sqrt[1 - tw2/kappaRq^2]) (
      (-tw2/(6 kappaRq^2)) uqbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.uq
    + (1/2 - 2 tw2/(3 kappaRq^2)) uqbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.uq
    + (-tw2/(6 kappaRq^2)) dqbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq
    + (-1/2 + tw2/(3 kappaRq^2)) dqbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.dq
    )
  + (-kappaRl gw/Sqrt[1 - tw2/kappaRl^2]) (
      (tw2/(2 kappaRl^2)) lbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.l
    + (-1/2 + tw2/kappaRl^2) lbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.l
    + (tw2/(2 kappaRl^2)) vlbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.vl
    + 1/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].ProjP.NR
    )
  ] Zr[mu]
];

LTotal := LWpkin + LZrkin + LNRkin + LWRqq + LWRlnu + LZRff;

274: \section{Effective Left-Right Symmetric Model}\label{sec:theory}
275: The Effective LRSM field content consists of the usual SM states, the $\WR^\pm$ and $\ZR$ gauge bosons, 
276: which are aligned with their mass eigenstates, and three heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_i$, 
277: aligned with the RH chiral states.
278: 
279: In the LRSM, the $\WR$ chiral coupling to quarks are given by
280: \begin{eqnarray}
281:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-q-q'} = \frac{-\kappa_R^q g}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j=u,d,\dots}\overline{u}_i V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ d_j + \text{H.c.},
282:  \label{chcurrent}
283: \end{eqnarray}
284: Here, $u_i (d_j)$ is an up-(down-)type quark of flavor $i (j)$; 
285: $P_{R(L)} = \frac{1}{2}(1\pm\gamma^5)$ denotes the RH(LH) chiral projection operator; and
286: $V_{ij}^{\rm CKM'}$  is the RH Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix, which is related to the SM CKM matrix.
287: Throughout this study, we will assume five massless quarks and take both the SM and RH CKM matrices to be diagonal with unit entries.
288: $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha_{\rm EM}(M_Z)}/\sin\theta_W$ is the SM Weak coupling constant and 
289: $\kappa_{R}^{q}\in\mathds{R}$ is an overall normalization for the $\WR$ interaction strength.
290: 
291: For leptons, the $\WR$ coupling and leptonic mixing is parametrized by~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Han:2012vk}
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293:  \mathcal{L}_{\WR-\ell-\nu/N} = \frac{-\kappa_R^\ell g}{\sqrt{2}}
294:  \sum_{\ell=e,\mu,\tau}
295:  \left[
296:  \sum_{m=1}^3	\overline{\nu^{c}_m} X_{\ell m} ~+~
297:  \sum_{m'=1}^3	\overline{N_{m'}} Y_{\ell m'}
298:  \right] ~W_{R \mu}^+ \gamma^\mu P_R~ \ell^-+\text{H.c.}
299: \end{eqnarray}
300: The matrix $Y_{\ell m'} (X_{\ell m})$ quantifies the mixing between 
301: the heavy (light) neutrino mass eigenstate $N_{m'}~(\nu_{m})$
302: and the RH chiral state with corresponding lepton flavor $\ell$. 
303: 
304: The mixing scale as~\cite{Keung:1983uu}
305: \begin{equation}
306: \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(1) \quad\text{and}\quad  
307: \vert X_{\ell m}\vert^2 \sim 1 - \vert Y_{\ell m'}\vert^2 \sim \mathcal{O}(m_{\nu_m}/m_{N_{m'}}).
308: \end{equation}
309: As in the quark sector, $\kappa_R^\ell\in\mathds{R}$ independently normalizes the $\WR$ coupling strength to leptons.
310: 
311: At TeV collider scales, both light neutrino masses and light neutrino mixing can be taken to zero.
312: So for simplicity, we take $Y_{\ell m'}$ to  be diagonal with unit entires:
313: \begin{equation}
314:   \vert Y_{e N}\vert = \vert Y_{\mu N_2}\vert = \vert Y_{\tau N_3}\vert = 1, \quad \vert Y_{\rm others}\vert = \vert X_{\ell m}\vert = 0.
315:   \label{eq:lrsmNuMixing}
316: \end{equation}
317: 
318: Mass and mixing assumptions are modifiable in the public model files~\cite{nloFRModel} but requires UFO regeneration.
319: Specifically, do not load the FR restrictions, ``massless.rst'' and ``diagonalCKM.rst''.

345: After LR symmetry breaking, the $W_{R}^{3}$ and $X_{(B-L)}$ gauge states mix and
346: give rise to the massive $Z_{R}$ and massless (hypercharge) $B$ bosons.
347: 
348: Subsequently, all fermions with $(B-L)$ charges, including $\nu_L$ and $N_R$, couple to $\ZR$.
349: 
350: For chiral fermion $f$, we parametrize the $\ZR$ neutral currents by
351: \begin{eqnarray}
352:  \mathcal{L}_{\ZR-f-f} &=& \frac{-\kappa_{R}^f g}{\sqrt{1 - \left(1/\kappa_{R}^f\right)^2\tWSq}}\sum_{f=u,e,\dots}
353:  \overline{f} Z_{R \mu} \gamma^\mu \left(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}P_L + g_{R}^{\ZR,f}P_R\right)f.
354: \label{neucurrent}
355: \end{eqnarray}
356: $\kappa_{R}^{f}$ are the same $\kappa_{R}^{q,\ell}$ as for $\WR$.
357: In terms of electric and isospin charges, the chiral coefficients are
358: \begin{eqnarray}
359:  g_{L}^{\ZR,f} &=& \left(T_{L}^{3,f} - Q^f\right)\frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq,
360:  \\
361:  g_{R}^{\ZR,f} &=& T_{R}^{3,f} - \frac{1}{\kappa_{R}^{f~2}}\tWSq Q^f.
362: \end{eqnarray}
363: SU$(2)_L$, SU$(2)_R$, and U$(1)_{\rm EM}$ quantum number assignments for $f$ are summarize in Tbl.~\ref{tb:qNumbers}.
364: 
365: For generic $\kappa_R^{q,\ell}$ normalizations, the LO $\WR,\ZR$ partial decay widths are then
366: \begin{eqnarray}
367:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{qq'}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
368:  \\
369:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb} 	&=& N_c \vert V^{\rm{CKM'}}_{tb}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{q 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
370: 					    \left(1-r_t^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_t^{\WR}\right),
371:  \\
372:  \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \ell N_{m'}} 	&=&     \vert Y_{\ell N_{m'}}\vert^2 \frac{\kappa_{R}^{\ell 2} g^2 \MWR}{48 \pi}
373: 					\left(1-r_N^{\WR}\right)^2\left(1+\frac{1}{2}r_N^{\WR}\right),
374: \\
375:  \Gam{\ZR\rightarrow f\overline{f}} &=&   
376:  N_c^f 
377:  \cfrac{\kappa_{\ZR}^{f 2} g^2 \MZR \sqrt{1-4r_f^{\ZR}}}{48\pi\left[1 - (1/\kappa_{R}^f)^2\tWSq\right]}
378:  \nonumber\\
379:  &\times&
380:  \left[(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}+g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1+2r_f^{\ZR})+(g_{L}^{\ZR,f}-g_{R}^{\ZR,f})^2(1-4r_f^{\ZR})\right]
381:  \\
382:  r_i^{V_R} &=& \frac{m_{i}^2}{M_{V_R}^2}.
383: \end{eqnarray}
384: Assuming diagonal quark mixing and lepton mixing in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lrsmNuMixing}), the total $\WR,\ZR$ widths are then
385: \begin{eqnarray}
386:  \Gamma_{\WR} &=& 2\Gam{\WR \rightarrow q\overline{q'}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow tb} 
387:  + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow e N_{1}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \mu N_{2}} + \Gam{\WR \rightarrow \tau N_{3}}
388:  \\
389:  \Gamma_{\ZR} &=& \sum_{f} \Gam{\ZR\rightarrow f\overline{f}}
390: \end{eqnarray}
